about: Launch-day guide (2026-11-19): names, descriptions and grades are the official PlayStation list as published by Exophase; numeric targets are the counters PSNProfiles tracks. Strategy text is our own advice derived from those official descriptions and is not yet verified in the game. Hidden flags follow PSNProfiles' secret-trophy view (28 hidden).

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum has no condition of its own: it unlocks when the other 54 trophies are earned, so the whole roadmap is the guide to it. Clear the missable flags before the finale, finish the story, then sweep the collectibles and activity counters. Requirement per the official Exophase list; nothing extra is listed.
steps: Earn the other 54 trophies
Check the Missables page before the final mission
Verify A Long Road (100%) is earned

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Gone Fishing is the mission the official list puts first, so treat it as the opening job and play it normally — the trophy is for completing it, not for any optional objective. Story-completion trophies like this one cannot be skipped. Our reading of the official description; not yet checked in the game.
steps: Start the story and play the opening mission
Finish Gone Fishing to pop the trophy

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Chapter 1 completion is automatic story progress: keep playing missions until the chapter closes. While you are in the opening stretch, keep an eye out for the Ocean Beach cocktail moment (In The Beginning…) — its description reads like an early-story beat. Advice from the official descriptions, unverified at launch.
steps: Complete every Chapter 1 mission
Watch for the Ocean Beach cocktail moment while nearby

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Chapter 2's trophy pops on chapter completion, so no side objective is required. The name keeps PlayStation's asterisks; the requirement is simply finishing the chapter. Between chapters is a good window to try one of each activity type for Master of None. Our advice from the official list, not yet verified in-game.
steps: Play through Chapter 2
Use the free-roam gaps to sample activity types

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 3 and the trophy is yours — it is tied to story progress, not to performance. The chapter title suggests the story reaches Vice City proper here, a natural point to start exploring districts for The Goodtime State. Reading of the official description; unverified at launch.
steps: Finish Chapter 3
Begin district exploration as the map opens up

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Chapter 4 is the last numbered chapter trophy, so finishing it should leave only the final mission on the story path. Before pushing on, sweep any contact strands you have unlocked — their finale trophies are easier while the contacts are still active. Advice derived from the official descriptions, not yet checked in the game.
steps: Complete Chapter 4
Finish unlocked contact strands before the finale

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: The gold story trophy is for completing the final mission. Our advice: treat it as a point of no return until proven otherwise — finish partner-dependent trophies (Hot Together, Retail Therapy) and the flagged one-time moments first, and keep a manual save beforehand. The official description names no choice or condition; this caution is our own, unverified at launch.
steps: Clear the Missables page first
Make a manual save before the finale
Complete the final mission

sources.label: Exophase — You Gotta Know When to Get Off

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Breakfast Run is a named story mission; completing it earns Trust, with no optional objective mentioned in the official text. Play it as the story presents it. If the game offers mission replays, a failed run can simply be retried — a series convention we expect but cannot confirm yet.
steps: Reach Breakfast Run in the story
Complete the mission

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: The Cartel Heist is a story heist mission, and the trophy is for completing it — the official description ties it to completion, not to a take size or approach. GTA heists have historically offered approach choices; nothing published says a choice locks this trophy, so any successful completion should count. Our advice, unverified in-game.
steps: Progress the story to The Cartel Heist
Complete the heist by any offered approach

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Child's Play is a named story mission; finish it and Family Matters unlocks. The description lists no stealth, timing or choice requirement, so a normal completion is the whole task. Reading of the official Exophase entry; not yet verified in the game.
steps: Reach Child's Play in the story
Complete the mission

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Headliners is a story mission and DWNFALL is its completion trophy. Nothing in the official description suggests an alternate outcome that skips it. Keep progressing the main thread; if you fail the mission, retry it rather than abandoning it. Our advice from the official list, unverified at launch.
steps: Reach Headliners in the story
Complete the mission, retrying if needed

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: VCIA Takedown is the story's airport job — VCIA reads as Vice City's international airport — and completing it earns Hi-Jacked. While you are at the airport, look for the chance to make an unscheduled departure (Catch Me If You Can); the two descriptions pair naturally. That pairing is our inference, not a confirmed fact.
steps: Complete VCIA Takedown
Try an unscheduled airport departure while there

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Operation Savage Glory is a named story mission; Snow Storm pops on completion. The official text gives no extra condition, so treat it as straight story progress. Our advice: keep a manual save before big missions so any one-time moment inside them can be retried. Unverified at launch.
steps: Reach Operation Savage Glory
Complete the mission

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: The second gold is the game's own 100% completion stat, which PSNProfiles tracks as a 0/100 counter. The official list does not publish what feeds that stat, so our advice is to finish everything else first — story, strands, collectibles, activities — then check the in-game completion screen for leftovers. What exactly counts is unverified at launch; the counter target is from PSNProfiles.
steps: Complete the story and all strands
Finish collectibles and activity counters
Check the in-game 100% screen for leftovers

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: A long-haul silver: 250 stunts, with PSNProfiles tracking the count to 250. The description does not define what registers as a stunt, so our advice is to treat jumps, wheelies and near-miss driving as candidates and watch the counter move — then farm whichever action counts. Do it in free roam after the story so nothing is time-pressed. Definition unverified at launch; target from PSNProfiles.
steps: Find which actions increment the stunt counter
Farm them in free roam
Track progress to 250 in this app

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: PSNProfiles tracks this as 0/9, so the game counts nine activity types. The official description says try each once — no wins or scores needed. Our advice: early in free roam, sample one of everything you find (races, fishing, arcade, ranges, drone races, bowling and the like) and tick them off; the exact roster of nine is unverified at launch.
steps: Discover the activity types on the map
Try each of the 9 once
Tick them off as the counter climbs

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: The silver asks for gold medals across the Shooting Range challenges, and PSNProfiles counts 42 of them. Medals usually score accuracy and time, so our advice is to learn each challenge's layout, then replay for gold rather than settling for a pass. Which weapons each challenge allows is unverified at launch; the 42 count is from PSNProfiles.
steps: Locate the Shooting Range
Learn each of the 42 challenges
Replay until every medal is gold

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Top Fun drone races appear at 14 locations per the PSNProfiles counter, and you must win at each — not merely enter. Our advice: visit every race spot once for Master of None, note which ones you lost, and return to those; drone handling is usually the skill gate, so practice the tightest course first. Location list unverified at launch; count from PSNProfiles.
steps: Find all 14 drone race locations
Win at least one race at each
Revisit any location where you only placed

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Twenty race wins, and the word different matters: repeating one race likely will not count, since PSNProfiles tracks 20 distinct wins. Our advice is to win once at each race venue you find, mixing street, off-road and water events if offered, rather than grinding a single easy loop. Whether repeats count is unverified at launch; the target is from PSNProfiles.
steps: Map out the race venues
Win 20 different races
Avoid relying on repeats of one race

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Cal offers a fishing challenge, and the trophy is for beating him — a head-to-head, not just catching fish. Our advice: take the challenge when Cal offers it and treat it as a timed contest; if you lose, ask for a rematch rather than walking away. Whether rematches are always available is unverified at launch; the requirement is the official Exophase description.
steps: Find Cal and accept his fishing challenge
Out-fish him to win
Rematch if the first attempt fails

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: One completed arcade game is enough — the description says an arcade game, not all of them. Our advice: find any arcade cabinet in free roam and play one game to its end; if completion means finishing a level rather than just credits, pick the easiest cabinet. What complete means here is unverified at launch; requirement per Exophase.
steps: Locate an arcade cabinet
Play one game through to completion

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Andy is one of the named contacts with a mission strand, and this bronze is for finishing his last job. Our advice: keep doing Andy's missions as they unlock instead of saving them all for post-game, since contact strands can be gated by story progress. Whether strands expire is unverified at launch; the requirement is the official description.

Complete every Andy mission through the finale

The name hints at a boat job, so expect water handling somewhere in the strand — our advice is to keep a boat accessible while working for him. That hint is our inference from the title, not a confirmed detail; requirement per Exophase.

Complete his final mission

The title suggests moving goods, so expect delivery-style jobs; our advice is to keep a fast, durable vehicle handy while working his thread. Complete his final mission

trophies.guide: Tyrone's last mission closes his strand and pops Spin On This!. Keep his thread moving alongside the story so the finale is available well before the endgame. The official description lists no condition beyond completion; our ordering advice is our own and unverified at launch.

Complete Tyrone's final mission

Our advice is to sweep them alongside the WAiNK locations and district exploration in one post-story loop, marking each spot in this tracker's counter as you go. The spot locations are not published yet; the 18 count is from PSNProfiles.

Whatever the WAiNK action turns out to be, 100 spots means a map-wide sweep — our advice is to do it in the same post-story loop as meditation spots and districts, checking off regions one at a time so none is double-backtracked. Overlap unverified at launch; count from PSNProfiles.

Our advice: attempt it during a stretch where the story has you working as a duo — raise the heat together, then break line of sight and stay out of the search cones until the stars fade. Mechanics unverified at launch; requirement per Exophase.

We flag it potentially missable for the same partner-window reason as Hot Together. Our advice: plan a short route between three nearby shops, keep the heat moderate so you survive the chain, and do it while the duo is together. Unverified at launch; requirement per Exophase.
